messages:
sasha: quick follow-up on the lease revamp RFC — thanks for the reviews earlier. I want to sync on a couple of tradeoffs before we land the API change.
ran: SG. Which tradeoffs are you most worried about?
sasha: mainly two: 1) semantics of fast-release vs deferred-release (impact on eviction pressure), 2) NUMA affinity hints and how heavy they should be in the public API.
maria: for (1) we should avoid a synchronous global scan on release. fast-release should mark stale and let background reclaimer do the heavy lifting. otherwise we blow tail latency under bursty demotes.
devon: Agree. Implementation note: mark -> queue -> async reclaim. Keep the fast path < 200ns.
kevin: for NUMA hinting: tenants already have locality skew. Exposing fine-grained NUMA controls invites misuse. Can we keep it as a soft hint that the runtime can ignore?
sasha: that's my preference too. API idea: lease_acquire(tenant, flags) where flags is an opt-in slug: [SOFT_NUMA_LOCALITY, HIGH_RETENTION]. Flags are advisory only.
ran: can you sketch expected lifecycle? e.g.:
```\n// pseudo\nh = lease_acquire(tid, flags);\nuse_memory(h);\nlease_release(h); // fast path: O(1)\n// background: reclaimer drains queue and unpins pages\n```\nmaria: looks good. We should add a per-tenant backpressure counter so the reclaimer can prioritize hot tenants. Otherwise a noisy tenant will delay reclaim for quiet ones.
devon: +1. Also suggest a compactness_score on the lease to prefer coalescing smaller slabs from low-score leases first.
kevin: one more: what about cross-tenant slab ownership? Are we doing hard isolation or soft sharing? current Dedicated customers expect strong isolation.
sasha: design proposal: by default soft-sharing with quotas; enterprise flag to opt-into strict islandization. That keeps the simple path for most use-cases and gives us a route to stricter semantics for regulated customers.
ran: sounds reasonable. Ops question: how would this affect metrics / SLOs?
sasha: we expose per-tenant resident_count, lease_queue_len, reclaim_latency_p50/p95. Reclaim backpressure increments when queue_len > threshold.
kevin: migrations: if we demote a GPU, how do leases behave across nodes? We need a lightweight lease-serial that survives move operations.
maria: lease_handle should carry a 64-bit epoch + tenant-id. Move = increment epoch and issue a move-event; old handles become stale. No distributed lock needed.
devon: implementation caveat: stale handles still referenced by in-flight work. we'll keep a grace window where stale handles are accepted for reads but new allocations fail fast with ESTALE.
ran: can we add a tiny test harness in the runtime tests that fuzzes release vs deferred-reclaim to catch races?
sasha: yes, I'll add a test matrix: fast-path baseline, forced-queue, tenant-move during reclaim.
ops-bot: deploy-check: lease-revamp branch passes unit tests (CI 2542) :white_check_mark:
sasha: thanks. action items: (1) I'll update the RFC with the API snippet + soft-hint semantics, (2) marie/ran please review the NUMA hint wording, (3) devon/kevin will draft the reclaimer prioritization plan. Back here in 24h? :thumbsup:
ran: yep.
maria: on it.
devon: will draft tomorrow morning.
kevin: will write migration edgecases doc.
